A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DINO-WM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated planning, generalization, reconstruction-quality and planner-comparison results across five environment suites, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Reacher evaluations, controlled ablations, timing measurements and planning visualizations.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen DINOv2 patch features, an action-conditioned causal transformer, latent prediction loss, an independently trained optional decoder and CEM/MPC planning. v2 clarifies removal of the transformer's tokenization layer and provides architecture details; it does not establish a changed proposed procedure. Decoder-loss and masking variants are ablation controls.

E1.justification: v2 adds Reacher, requiring a two-joint arm's entire pose to match a target image (Appendix A.1; Tables 1–2). This is a focused extension into articulated-arm pose control. The five existing environments and three generalization families remain; Maze is a shortened name for PointMaze.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain IRIS, DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, AVDC/AVDC-AC, R3M, ResNet and DINO CLS. Reacher extends existing comparator sets. The new masking and decoder-loss variants are controlled DINO-WM ablations, rather than newly introduced baseline methods.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands the experimental design with PushT dataset-size sweeps, history-length/masking controls, decoder-loss controls and a timing protocol using CEM with 100 samples and 10 optimization steps. Reacher uses 3,000 training trajectories and 50 evaluation instances. Appendix A.1 also revises Wall's reported training count from 2,000 to 1,920 trajectories, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 tests how performance depends on training-data quantity, whether causal masking prevents failures as history increases, and whether reconstruction-loss backpropagation helps the predictor. These provide substantial new analyses of data dependence and design choices beyond v1's retained encoder, planner and generalization comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The existing evaluation practice of 50 navigation/pushing instances and 10 deformable-object instances remains; additional result rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds Reacher results, including success rates of 0.92 for DINO-WM and 0.64 for DreamerV3, plus substantial ablation and timing results (Tables 5–7 and 10). DreamerV3's PushT score in Table 1 changes from 0.04 to 0.30; DINO-WM remains 0.90, while new ablation tables separately report 0.92. Existing generalization and planner scores are retained, and relocated LPIPS/SSIM results differ only by rounding.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, latent-model definitions, losses and planning equations are mathematically unchanged. The new 'Scaling Laws' subsection presents empirical trends, not a new formal law, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain offline task-agnostic world modeling, zero-shot visual-goal planning without reward models or inverse models, and generalization to unseen configurations. The introduction retains the 56% LPIPS and 45% planning-improvement claims. Expanded evaluations support these existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses difficulty obtaining sufficient state-action coverage in complex environments and proposes exploration and model updates. New ablation interpretations explain future-frame leakage without causal masking and benefits from richer training data. Section 3.2 replaces v1's gradient-terrain explanation for GD's weakness with a proposal to investigate regularization.

D1.justification: Appendices A.8–A.9 add substantial specifications: transformer depth, attention heads, parameter count, feature dimensions, image resizing, frame skips, trajectory lengths and timing hardware/settings. Section 4.2 clarifies offline, reward-free baseline training and MPC evaluation. Code/models change from promised release to reported open-source availability. Some details remain inconsistent: Table 11 lists five-step Rope/Granular trajectories while Appendix A.1 still states 20 steps.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Chain-of-Thought Predictive Control, Diffusion World Model, Manipulate by Seeing, Embed to Control and DeepMind Control Suite. These supplement existing context and benchmark attribution; the positioning against task-dependent and pixel-generative world models remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanatory passages are tightened, Section 4.1's environment descriptions are condensed, and metric discussion is redistributed between main text and appendix. The standalone reproducibility statement disappears, the ethics statement becomes an impact statement, and acknowledgments are added. The overall argument and main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text and references, redesigns the environment montage, and expands/reorders benchmark tables. The full LPIPS/SSIM table and planning-comparison visualizations move to the appendix. New ablation/timing tables and an all-six-environment trajectory figure accompany substantial resizing, relabeling and relocation of existing displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility by directly testing previously untested masking and decoder-loss choices, measuring data dependence and computational cost, and documenting architecture and preprocessing. These address important evidential and implementation gaps in v1. The gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including unexplained 0.90 versus 0.92 PushT reference scores and conflicting trajectory lengths; uncertainty reporting remains absent.
